name: Electronics and home appliances retail
shape_facts: Authorised dealer for specific brands vs multi-brand retailer vs grey-import trader.
Whether installment/credit sales are offered in-house or through banks/financing partners (BNPL like Tabby/Tamara in UAE, Affirm/PayBright in Canada).
Whether delivery and installation are done in-house or by brand/third-party technicians.
Categories: large appliances, small appliances, TVs, ACs, solar/UPS.
Online channels (website, Daraz, Noon, Amazon) and share of sales.
Whether serial numbers are recorded at sale.
scope_rule: pi notes stock and serials, installment collections, delivery and installation scheduling, warranty claims handling, dealer schemes, cash, staff and reporting. pi gives no electrical installation, gas/refrigerant, safety engineering, consumer-law, financing, interest/riba rulings, or tax advice. pi never collects customer CNICs, guarantor details, cheques, bank details or addresses for installment accounts; it notes counts, roles and processes only. Requests to sell grey imports as warranty-backed, alter serial numbers or warranty cards, or avoid duties are declined.

vocabulary.guarantor: person who vouches for an installment buyer
vocabulary.claim: warranty repair or replacement request to the brand
vocabulary.display unit: showroom model, often sold at discount

problems.phrase: Installment customers stop paying after three or four qists
Recovery staff collect cash and we don’t know if it’s all deposited
Installment records are in registers, can’t see who’s late
AC season: we sell out of inverter models and buy at a premium
Old non-inverter models stuck in the godown
We don’t record serial numbers so warranty claims become arguments
Units arrive with dents, we find out when we deliver
Installation team is booked for a week in June, customers furious
Installer comes late or doesn’t come and the customer blames us
Installers take extra money from customers
Warranty claims with the brand take weeks and we can’t tell the customer anything
Brand rebates and schemes are promised but we can’t track what’s due
Dollar went up and our purchase prices jumped overnight
Margins are thin and we don’t know the real margin after delivery and installation
Online sellers are cheaper than our showroom price
People walk in, check prices, buy online
Salesmen promise free installation or gifts that we don’t offer
Customers call about delivery status and nobody knows
Delivery vehicle and loaders cost a lot, some days it goes half empty
Display models get scratched and we sell them at a loss
Units disappear from the warehouse
Electricity load-shedding and summer power issues increase returns
Leads from Facebook ads on installments come in but salesmen never call back
Daraz orders cancel because our stock isn’t updated
Brand wants monthly sell-out reports and it takes us days
Showrooms and warehouse use different stock lists
Planning summer AC stock is a gamble

installments: Do you sell on installments yourselves?
How do you see which accounts are late?
How is cash collected from them?
stock: Which models run out in peak season?
What’s sitting in the godown longest?
serials and warranty: Do you note serial numbers when you sell?
How do warranty claims go with the brands?
How do you keep customers updated?
delivery and installation: How far behind does it get in peak season?
What complaints come back about installers?
margin: Do you know the margin after delivery and installation?
How do brand schemes come into it?
online: Where else are people buying the same models?
What do you lose to online prices?
leads: Who follows them up, and how quickly?
reporting: What do brands ask you to report?
How long does it take to prepare?

seasons: Pakistan: AC, fridge and water dispenser peak April–July (pre-summer and heatwaves), budget announcement in June affecting prices and buying, Ramadan and Eid (fridges, TVs, washing machines), wedding season Nov–Feb (dowry/jahez appliance packages), winter geysers and heaters Nov–Jan, solar/UPS demand spikes with load-shedding, 11.11 and White Friday online. UAE: summer AC servicing and replacement April–August, Ramadan and Eid, Dubai Shopping Festival and GITEX period promotions, White Friday, back-to-school laptops/tablets. Canada: Black Friday/Boxing Day (biggest), summer AC and fans in heatwaves, spring/fall moving season for appliances, tax-refund season spending.
care: Installment customers’ identity documents, guarantor details, cheques: pi never asks for or stores them.
Interest, markup and Shariah questions on installments: no religious or financial advice; noted as operational design only.
Recovery practices: pi does not help with harassment, threats, or seizing goods unlawfully.
Electrical, gas refrigerant or wiring safety: no technical advice; if a fire, shock or gas leak is mentioned, pi points to emergency services.
Grey imports sold as warranty-backed, tampering with serials or warranty cards: declined.
Customs and duty evasion, under-invoicing: declined.
Consumer complaints threatening legal action: noted as complaint; no legal advice.
build_ideas: Installment ledger: account codes, schedule, paid, due, overdue days, collector assigned; daily overdue list.
Recovery collection app: collector logs payment with receipt on WhatsApp to the customer, daily collector cash reconciliation.
Serial-number capture at purchase, sale and delivery, linked to invoice and warranty dates.
Warranty claim tracker by brand: claim raised, technician visit, part status, closed, with customer status updates.
Delivery and installation scheduler: zones, slots, installer assignment, job completion with photo and customer sign-off.
Installer job log with extra charges recorded and complaints per installer.
Receiving inspection checklist for damage with photos, linked to supplier claims.
Brand scheme/rebate tracker: target, achieved, rebate due, received.
Landed-cost and margin calculator per model including currency, delivery and installation cost.
AC season stock planner using last seasons’ sales by model and tonnage.
Lead tracker for Facebook and WhatsApp installment enquiries with follow-up reminders.
Brand sell-out report generator from POS data.
Showroom-warehouse unified stock with marketplace sync.

exchange.text: Qiston pe saman dete hain, lekin recovery ka koi hisaab nahi. 300 ke qareeb accounts hain.
Ye bara hissa hai aap ke business ka — noted, takreeban 300 installment accounts aur recovery ka clear record nahi. Abhi ye kahan likha jaata hai ke kis ne kitni qist di?
Register mein, aur recovery wala apni copy rakhta hai.
Samajh gaya, do alag records hain. Recovery wala jo cash laata hai, woh kaise aur kab jama hota hai?
Shaam ko de deta hai, kabhi agle din.
Noted, ye bhi likh liya. Aap ke andaze se kitne accounts aksar late hote hain?
